title: Mid-South Plant Services v. Dresser-Rand
summary: Repeated performance under conflicting labor-supply forms produced a disputed inference about the governing terms.
notes: The majority treated the supplier as accepting the customer’s refusal of a non-solicitation clause through continuing to supply labor. The dissent argued that the competing inference should be evaluated by a jury rather than resolved on summary judgment. The note is a useful link between formation facts, interpretation, and procedural posture.
